source.title: DuplexJail: Spoken Interruption Attacks on Full-Duplex Speech Models
source.authors: Jaechul Roh; Deepak Chandran; Amir Houmansadr; Andrea Fanelli

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether spoken interruption prompts can raise harmful responses in full-duplex speech models, extending the opening-bypass question to spoken interaction.
record.gate_note: The study tests spoken prompts delivered at different times, including a prompt explicitly named Spoken Prefilling. It does not edit assistant output tokens; the authors distinguish their method from editing those tokens. Table 2 prompt-screening results, the Procedural Completion rows in Table 3, and the Figure 2 timing sweep are not extracted here because of the 60-row limit. No results test fine-tuning, per-token KL, localized weights, or safety-deepening training.
record.test_reason: No version is tested. V4 covers prefilling the assistant's own compliant start, adversarial suffixes or decoding changes. Here fixed spoken prompts arrive through the user audio channel, and the authors say they do so 'without editing the assistant's output tokens'. The measure is whole-response ASR, which the authors say is not a refusal-to-harm transition rate. The post-response control (prompt given after the response ends) gives gains close to mid-response interruption, so the effect is not shown to depend on getting past the refusal opening. This is a user-turn spoken jailbreak in a new modality and is recorded under fits_no_version. The study cites Qi et al. (an original source) as inspiration for the prompts.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also say the fixed-delay advantage over timing controls holds on AdvBench but not consistently on HarmBench. They stress that ASR measures whole-response harmfulness, not refusal-to-harm transitions, and that BayLing decreases may reflect truncated output rather than stronger safety.
record.recipe_differences: This is a spoken full-duplex interruption attack, not fine-tuning or editing assistant output tokens. It delivers fixed prompts through the user audio channel at request-relative delays or after a refusal cue; it also tests timing controls.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by model, benchmark, spoken prompt, and delivery timing. Guided Completion has substantial increases for PersonaPlex models; FLM-Audio varies by prompt and timing; BayLing-Duplex shows decreases in the reported fixed-delay and control conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Fixed spoken jailbreak prompts injected through the user audio channel during generation raise whole-response ASR for PersonaPlex/PersonaPlex-RL: Guided Completion +9.5 to +39.3 pp. FLM-Audio is mostly near baseline, except Spoken Prefilling at 0.5 s (+10.3/+13.7 pp). BayLing-Duplex falls below baseline in all fixed-delay conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In full-duplex speech models, user-channel spoken interruption prompts raise harmful compliance in a model- and timing-dependent way.

fits_no_version.finding: The same prompt given as a post-response follow-up gives gains close to mid-response interruption for the PersonaPlex family (+24.7/+28.5 pp AdvBench, +12.7/+13.7 HarmBench). Mid-response delivery beats the controls on AdvBench only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Much of the spoken-prompt effect does not depend on interrupting the model's opening.

record.problems: Whole-response ASR is not a measure of refusal-to-harm transitions; the authors explicitly distinguish these. ASR includes trials without interruption, and some control effects include many uninterrupted trials. Only three decoding runs are reported. Decreased ASR may reflect suppressed or truncated audible output rather than stronger safety. The supplied text reports no uncertainty test beyond standard deviations.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 Procedural Completion results, Table 2 single-run prompt screening, and Figure 2 fixed-delay sweep are omitted because the 60-row cap was reached after keeping the two principal prompt conditions, all reported Guided Completion timing controls, and the model/benchmark/timing variation for those conditions.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or position analysis.
Assistant-token prefilling, adversarial suffixes and decoding changes are not tested; no refusal-to-harm transition rate is measured.
No analysis of the cause of shallowness.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's states have minor inconsistencies: changes within SD (e.g., -1.0, +0.7, +1.0 pp) are coded reversed or partial. Prompt screening (Table 2) was done on PersonaPlex/AdvBench, so those Table 3 cells are in-sample. Only three decoding runs per condition.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and its effect on refusal.
Benign-data fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.
Textual prefill of assistant output tokens, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes are not tested; the study tests spoken interruption prompts, including Spoken Prefilling.
Whether safety behavior is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether data or training objectives produce shallow safety behavior.
Training to deepen safety across response tokens and its robustness.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: PersonaPlex and PersonaPlex-RL, both benchmarks, Guided Completion and Spoken Prefilling conditions, plus request-end and post-response controls
reader_labels.reason: Harmful-response rates rise over baseline, but remain partial rather than showing safety behavior fully defeated; see the associated rows.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: FLM-Audio with Spoken Prefilling, fixed-delay 0.5 s on AdvBench and HarmBench, and refusal-triggered on HarmBench
reader_labels.reason: These settings raise ASR, but the increases are condition-specific and do not hold across the other tested FLM-Audio conditions.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: FLM-Audio with Guided Completion on AdvBench and HarmBench; Spoken Prefilling at fixed-delay 1.0 s and refusal-triggered on AdvBench, and fixed-delay 1.0 s on HarmBench
reader_labels.reason: These conditions show no increase or a decrease from baseline, rather than a consistent bypass.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: BayLing-Duplex, all reported fixed-delay conditions and request-end/post-response controls
reader_labels.reason: Reported ASR is below baseline in every included BayLing-Duplex condition.
